review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent planning expectation for the original PRD and frozen inputs. REQ-001, AC-001 through AC-003, the two exact writable owner paths, and the implementation/independent-verification task split agree with the specification. The source establishes that exposeHeaders currently accepts only a static array and is resolved outside the request handler, supporting the requested per-request synchronous/asynchronous callback change. The existing test file is included in tsconfig.spec.json and the Vitest configuration; package.json explicitly runs compiler checking before runtime tests. Build configuration establishes that public declarations are generated from source, so no separately maintained declaration owner or release-configuration edit is required. The feature is invocation-local and does not require shared-data or persistent-state impacts; pending data.change and domain.state claims therefore do not invalidate the eligible-agent expectations. The designated implementer and verifier have appropriate roles, availability, and relevant active trusted capability claims, and a separate configured project reviewer satisfies the earlier review prerequisite. No unresolved material DEC-001 or hypothetical C input is present in this case. Ready status and empty blocking reasons are appropriate planning expectations, not authorization to dispatch work. Repository identity, base commit, evidence fingerprints, and the frozen source/team/decision/model/policy release-input fields are consistent as supplied; the different source-digest domains and PRD trimming are explicitly accounted for. Historical operations are identified as old-bundle records rather than candidate evidence for this bundle. This review relies on the supplied Service-bound fingerprints and provenance; I did not recompute digests, execute code, or provide human attestation.
